inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement share-based payment add-back (EUR313m). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; Sanofi's plans are predominantly performance shares with treasury-share delivery, so the add-back is taken as the full charge.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 weighted-average shares (1,196.6m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The count has actually been FALLING ~2%/yr on buybacks (EUR5bn 2025, EUR1bn 2026 completed) -- the flat count is therefore funded and conservative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC: risk-free 3.2% (10y French OAT), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.8 (mega-cap defensive pharma) -> 7.2% CoE; +1.0pp pipeline/patent-cliff concentration premium (Dupixent ~36% of sales, tolebrutinib CRL + amlitelimab discontinuation killed both intended successors, brand-new CEO) -> 8.2% CoE; blended with ~2.7% after-tax debt cost at ~11% weight (net debt EUR11.0bn vs EUR92bn market cap, Aa3/AA) -> 7.6%, rounded to 7.5%. CAVEAT -- the 'charged once' claim does NOT hold in this build. The +1.0pp concentration premium is in the WACC AND the same Dupixent cliff/pipeline risk is what raised the bear weight from the 15% house default to 25%. Section 7f allows either lever, not both for the same risk. Removing the premium (WACC 6.5%) lifts base IV to ~EUR110.7; keeping it and reverting the bear weight to 15% lifts weighted IV to ~EUR103. The published EUR97.35 is therefore the conservative end of a defensible range, but it is double-counted, not 'charged once'.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (10-year component build) -- conventional operating pharma, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco. OPERATING ANCHOR: business (non-GAAP) earnings, not IFRS net income -- IFRS NI is distorted by disposal gains (FY2020 Regeneron stake, FY2025 Opella) and acquisition amortization/impairments; FY2025 business operating income EUR12,149m (27.8% margin), business EPS EUR7.83. FCF BASE: statutory OCF-capex EUR7,212m minus SBC EUR313m = owner FCF EUR6,899m (15.8% of sales). The company's own EUR9.9bn 'FCF' is BEFORE restructuring, which for Sanofi is a recurring ~EUR1-2bn/yr cash cost -- the model uses the statutory series. EBITDA CALIBRATION: the 'adj EBITDA margin' driver is a CASH-EBITDA margin, i.e. business EBITDA (~35% of sales FY2025) net of ~4.5-5.5pp of recurring restructuring / litigation / other operating cash leakage, calibrated so the component build reproduces actual owner FCF (Y1 component margin 16.6% vs 15.8% FY2025 actual, the difference being the guided FY2026 margin expansion). CLIFF SHAPE: years 1-5 (2026-2030) ramp on guidance (FY2026 ~10% CER less ~1pp FX) toward the ~EUR56bn 2030 ambition; years 6-10 (2031-2035) model Dupixent LOE erosion (US patents ~2031+, ~36% of sales, 50/50 Regeneron profit share) with group revenue dipping negative mid-window; terminal growth only 1.0-2.0% because the terminal year sits beyond the cliff. TERMINAL: max(0,min(Gordon, cap x FCF10)), cap 15x base/bull and 12x bear (post-cliff pharma); the CAP binds in all three scenarios at the house WACC -- the model is NOT relying on a generous Gordon multiple. LEASES (IFRS 16): treatment A -- lease liabilities sit inside total debt/net debt (EUR11.0bn company-stated net debt reconciles with debt minus cash) and lease principal is NOT deducted from flows; ongoing lease renewal is inside the 7.0-8.1% capex path. NCI: immaterial (~EUR30m of a EUR7.8bn NI). Interest income NOT stripped: Sanofi is a net-DEBT company; there is no cash pile being double-counted.
inputs.balance_sheet_staleness_warning: NET DEBT IS STALE AND UNDERSTATED. EUR11,045m is the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, carried against an Aug-2026 price and Q2-2026 share count. Since that date Sanofi has paid: the EUR4.12 dividend (~EUR4.9bn, which a buyer today does NOT receive), the Dynavax acquisition (~EUR1.6bn, while Heplisav-B revenue is already inside the projected flows), and the EUR1bn buyback -- confirmed fully purchased by 2026-04-29 (Q2-2026 presentation, note 2) -- whose reduced share count the model DOES credit while the cash it consumed is absent from net debt. That last one is a genuine double-count in the model's favour. Partly offset by H1-2026 free cash flow. Directionally this overstates intrinsic value by low single-digit EUR/share; the H1-2026 balance sheet was not in the extracted filings on disk, so no figure is substituted here rather than guess one. REFRESH net_debt from the H1-2026 20-F/interim balance sheet before acting.
inputs.lease_treatment_note: UNRESOLVED. total_debt EUR18,702m is Sanofi's EX-LEASE borrowings figure, so the ~EUR1.7bn of IFRS-16 lease liabilities is charged NEITHER as debt in the bridge NOR as a rent expense in the flows -- i.e. treatment A is claimed but not implemented. Correcting it (either add leases to net debt, or deduct lease principal from owner FCF -- once, never both) reduces intrinsic value by roughly EUR1.4/share.
inputs.equity_bridge_omissions: Bridge is incomplete, net effect roughly +EUR1 to +EUR2/share in the model's favour once combined: (a) the retained 48.2% Opella stake (~EUR3bn, ~+EUR2.5/share, NOT counted -- understates value); (b) contingent consideration and the Beyfortus royalty liability (~-EUR1.2/share, not deducted); (c) shares are basic weighted-average 1,196.6m rather than fully diluted ~1,204m (~+EUR0.5/share of overstatement). Section 7 of the owner-FCF method requires non-operating assets and diluted shares in the bridge; this build omitted both.
inputs.da_pct_basis: da_pct 7.3% VERIFIED as cash-shielding depreciation, not inflated by acquisition intangibles. A reviewer argued it embeds ~EUR2.2bn of intangible amortization and should fall to 3.2%. Checked against source: Sanofi's FY2025 intangible amortization is EUR1,776m (SEC XBRL ifrs-full AmortisationIntangibleAssetsOtherThanGoodwill); the EUR2,241m the reviewer cited is FY2025 IMPAIRMENT (ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLoss...), a different line. Depreciation alone is ~EUR3.7bn (capex EUR3,538m less the disclosed -EUR162m 'capex net of depreciations' bridge) = 8.5% of sales, and total D&A is ~12.6%. So 7.3% sits BELOW depreciation alone and already excludes the intangible amortization. Lowering it to 3.2% would understate a real cash tax shield. NO CHANGE MADE.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance_blend: FY2026 ~10% CER (upgraded Jul-2026, ~-1pp FX) decelerating toward the ~EUR56bn 2030 sales ambition, i.e. ~5%/yr through 2030 -- then negative through the 2031+ Dupixent erosion window. Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor: book value is distorted by EUR5bn buybacks, the Opella disposal and FX in reserves. IFRS EPS CAGRs rejected: FY2020 (Regeneron stake gain) and FY2025 (Opella gain) endpoints are disposal-inflated.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR is NEGATIVE (-1.5%) vs revenue +5.0% -- divergence >30%. Cause is capital return and disposal accounting (EUR5bn 2025 buyback, Opella deconsolidation), not value destruction; growth anchor taken from guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported OCF-capex minus SBC) for all years. Owner-FCF margin history: FY2021 21.8%, FY2022 21.8%, FY2023 18.8%, FY2024 13.7% (Opella separation costs + capex ramp), FY2025 15.8%. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is negative (-5.6%) while revenue grew +5.0% -- the gap is the US-onshoring capex ramp (EUR2.1bn FY2021 -> EUR3.5bn FY2025) and elevated restructuring, both explicitly in the component build rather than extrapolated. CALIBRATION CAVEAT: the FY2025 owner-FCF margin of 15.8% (EUR6,899m) is flattered by a ~EUR2.1bn one-off working-capital inflow inside the EUR10,750m statutory OCF; ex that, the underlying margin is ~11.0%. The forward margin path is built from components (EBITDA margin, capex, tax, WC) and stands on its own logic, but the claim that Y1 is 'calibrated' to a 15.8% actual overstates the quality of that anchor.

valuation_philosophy.operating_anchor: Business (non-GAAP) earnings are the operating anchor. IFRS net income is unusable across this history: FY2017 (+EUR4bn animal-health swap gain), FY2020 (+Regeneron stake sale), FY2025 (+Opella gain) are disposal-inflated while other years carry acquisition amortization and impairments. FY2025 business operating income EUR12,149m / business EPS EUR7.83 describe the actual drug business; the DCF's cash-EBITDA margin driver is business EBITDA net of recurring restructuring cash so it ties to statutory owner FCF.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value: The terminal value is deliberately patent-cliff-constrained. Dupixent is ~36% of sales, targeted at ~EUR25bn by 2030, profit-shared 50/50 with Regeneron, with key US patents running to ~2031+. A 10-year explicit window therefore crosses the erosion front: the model ramps to ~EUR56bn sales by 2030, then takes group revenue NEGATIVE for 2032-2034 as biosimilars erode the franchise, and only then capitalizes at 1.0-2.0% terminal growth with a 12-15x FCF cap. The cap binds in every scenario -- no scenario relies on a Gordon multiple the market would not pay for post-cliff pharma. STATE PLAINLY: because the 7.5% WACC makes the Gordon value exceed the cap in ALL three scenarios (terminal_value_binding = 'cap' everywhere), the stated terminal growth rates of 1.0-2.0% do NOTHING to the result -- the sensitivity grid rows are flat across terminal growth at WACC <= 7.5% for exactly this reason. The real terminal assumption is '15x FCF (12x bear)', not a growth rate.
valuation_philosophy.why_upside_is_credible: Base IV EUR102 (+33%) implies P/B 1.72 (10y avg 1.59, max 1.84), P/S 2.81 (avg 2.84) and 13.1x business EPS -- multiples Sanofi itself traded at repeatedly this decade. The stock sits in the lower half of its 10y price range (EUR64.7-104.4) at 1.35x book, its decade low, while business EPS grew +22.7% in H1-2026. The upside is a discount unwinding to Sanofi's own history, not a re-rating to US-pharma multiples.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands the upgraded guidance (~10% CER, ~-1pp FX -> +9% reported; margin +1pp on gross-margin mix). 2027-2030 decelerates 5% -> 3.5% as Dupixent ramps to ~EUR25bn, launches (Ayvakit, ALTUVIIIO, Sarclisa, Wayrilz) reach ~EUR10bn and vaccines stay roughly flat at ~EUR9bn -- landing ~EUR56bn in 2030, consistent with the raised ambition. Cash-EBITDA margin expands 30.5% -> 32% on operating leverage and restructuring wind-down. 2031-2035: Dupixent US LOE erosion takes group revenue -2/-3% in 2032-33 before launches and pipeline replace the hole; margin gives back ~2pp as the highest-margin franchise shrinks. Tax 21% throughout (FY2026 guidance). Terminal 1.5% growth, 15x FCF cap binding.

bull.narrative: Dupixent beats the EUR25bn ambition (new indications: COPD ramp, CSU, bullous pemphigoid; Q4W dosing extends the franchise) and lifecycle management plus the 50/50 Regeneron alliance blunts the 2031+ cliff to a plateau rather than a decline. Garijo's R&D reset works: the launch cohort (+61% YoY at Q2-2026) exceeds EUR10bn, Blueprint/Dynavax deals deliver, and US policy (tariffs settled by onshoring commitments, MFN diluted) does not bite. Margin reaches 33%; erosion years are 0/-1% not -2/-3%; terminal 2.0%, 15x cap still binding.

bear.narrative: The three live US policy risks bite together: Section 232 tariffs raise the cost base, IRA/MFN pricing compresses Dupixent US net pricing, and ACIP/vaccine-policy turmoil keeps vaccines in decline (2030 ambition already cut to EUR9bn). Ebglyss and Tezspire take atopic-derm/asthma share so Dupixent peaks nearer EUR20bn, and with tolebrutinib and amlitelimab already dead the pipeline cannot refill -- the 2031-34 cliff is steeper (-5/-6%) and margin erodes to 26% as the mix degrades. Tax drifts to 23% (Pillar 2 + US onshoring). Terminal 1.0% growth, 12x cap for a structurally shrinking post-cliff pharma.

entry_price.method: PV at the 15% hurdle of the 10 interim owner FCFs plus a terminal value REBUILT AT THE HURDLE RATE -- min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF10) -- less net debt, per share; per scenario, then probability-weighted. The terminal value is NOT the WACC-built one: discounting the flows at 15% while valuing the exit at 7.5% assumes you sell to a buyer accepting half your required return, and it imports a 15x cap chosen as a brake on Gordon runaway at 7.5% (at 15% Gordon is only ~7.5x). Corrected 2026-09-01.
entry_price.note: Weighted 15%-IRR entry EUR43.12 sits ~44% below the current EUR76.81. A hurdle entry near half of intrinsic value is expected for a business discounted at 7.5%, not a red flag. The previously published EUR56.32 was overstated ~31% by the WACC-built-terminal-value error.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF10)), so flows and exit are charged the same rate. The 15% row ties to entry_price.base.entry_price and the 7.5% row to valuation.base.intrinsic_value. The earlier version held TV at the 7.5% WACC and varied only the discounting, overstating every row. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. Flat cells occur where the 15x FCF terminal cap binds (everywhere at WACC <= 7.5%), so terminal growth stops mattering -- the cap is doing its job of preventing Gordon runaway at low discount rates.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: BOTH intended Dupixent successors failed inside 8 months (tolebrutinib CRL Dec-2025, amlitelimab dropped Jul-2026), the board removed the CEO over it, and three US policy risks (232 tariffs, IRA/MFN, vaccine policy) are live simultaneously. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs pipeline recovery AND policy calm AND Dupixent lifecycle extension to hold together. Base 50%: guidance momentum (H1-2026 business EPS +22.7%, guidance upgraded) makes the near-term path well-evidenced; the dispute is about 2031+. NOTE: this bear weight and the +1.0pp WACC concentration premium both price the same Dupixent cliff/pipeline-failure risk -- see inputs.wacc_rationale. Charged twice; the model is conservative rather than wrong, but the two levers should not be read as independent.
probability_weighted.band_note: The house/street band is only ~EUR4.7/share wide because SBC is 0.7% of sales -- this is nearly an SBC-zero name. band_position is negative because the price sits BELOW the house (fully-SBC-expensed) value entirely; the market is not paying even the strictest basis.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trips. Base IV EUR102.45 implies P/B 1.72 (below the 1.84 max, near the 1.59 avg), P/Sales 2.81 (below the 2.84 avg), 13.1x business EPS (below the 21.3 adj-P/E avg) and 14.5x the IFRS-proxy EBITDA (above the 12.3 avg but well below the 20.6 max; on business EBITDA it is only 8.7x -- the IFRS proxy is depressed by acquisition amortization/impairments in FY2025). Base upside is +32.6% -- nowhere near the >100% trip threshold -- and the price sits in the LOWER half of the 10y EUR64.68-104.40 range, at the decade-low 1.35x book. Every implied multiple is one the market has repeatedly paid for this exact company.

screening.verdict: UNDERVALUED on the weighted basis (+27% to EUR97.35 vs EUR76.81), but well below the 15% hurdle entry (EUR43.12 weighted, corrected 2026-09-01 from a mis-stated EUR56.32). On a terminal value rebuilt at each required return, today's price implies a ~9-10% forward IRR on the base path -- not the ~11% previously reported, which was flattered by holding the exit value at the 7.5% WACC. A EUR3.92 dividend (~5.1% yield, 31 consecutive increases) is paid while waiting and is not separately capitalized in the FCF model. Caveats that all cut the same way: net debt is stale by eight months and excludes a paid dividend, the Dynavax cash and a completed buyback whose share count IS credited (inputs.balance_sheet_staleness_warning); IFRS-16 leases are charged neither way (~EUR1.4/share); and the 7.5% WACC is the single largest driver -- at the 9% house rate base IV is EUR86.4, not EUR102.45.
